title: PHARM · IV fluids in heart failure (ASSESS BEFORE YOU POUR) (high stakes, night shift, Smart Prep errors)
hook: Nurses: weak heart, BP 86/50. Open the fluids?
hook_backups: Nurses: low BP at 3 AM. A fluid bolus fixes it?
Nurses: BP 86/50 and she's asleep. Bolus now?
belief: Low blood pressure always means give fluids fast.

story.patient: 79-year-old woman with heart failure (a weak pump), admitted with a urinary infection; she had her evening blood pressure pills

timeline.beat: Automatic cuff: BP (blood pressure) 86/50. She's asleep. Patient and nurse in frame with the hook
'She's dry.' The IV (intravenous) saline goes wide open, 1 liter. Nobody listens to her lungs
timeline.mistake_line: Treated a number before assessing her

timeline.beat: No call, no order for the bolus
timeline.mistake_line: Gave a fluid bolus with no order

timeline.beat: Crackles, a wet cough, 'I can't lie flat.' 'Just a cold.' Fluids keep running

timeline.outcome: Fluid in her lungs. 3 mistakes. Every one avoidable.

caught_it.text: Recheck the BP by hand. Look at her: alert? dizzy?
Listen to her lungs, check swelling and urine, review tonight's BP pills
Call the provider with your findings. Fluids only as ordered, then reassess
Crackles or breathless on fluids: stop them, sit her up, oxygen, call

memory_line: Weak pump, low BP: assess before you pour.
caption_lesson:
🌙 Night shift, 3:05 AM. She's 79 with heart failure (a weak pump). She had her evening blood pressure pills.
• BP (blood pressure) 86/50 on the automatic cuff. Asleep

❌ 3 mistakes, 3 error types
1️⃣ Acted too soon: opened 1 liter of saline wide, never assessed her
2️⃣ Scope error: gave a fluid bolus with no order
3️⃣ Acted too late: crackles and a wet cough called "just a cold", fluids kept running
➡️ 4:10 AM: SpO2 (oxygen saturation) 84%, pink frothy sputum. Rapid response.

💧 IV (intravenous) fluids in heart failure (ASSESS BEFORE YOU POUR)
• A weak pump can't move extra fluid forward
• It backs up into the lungs: crackles, a wet cough, breathless lying flat
• A low BP has many causes. Find hers first

✅ The right move
• Recheck the BP by hand and look at her
• Listen to the lungs, check swelling and urine, review tonight's meds
• Call the provider. Fluids only as ordered, then reassess
• Crackles or breathless on fluids: stop them, sit her up, oxygen, call

🧠 Weak pump, low BP: assess before you pour.
share_line: 📤 Send this to the nurse who'd open the fluids before listening to the lungs.
